issues.failure_explanation: The H^1(I,H) norm is never defined. Proposition prop: XX properties only gives an isomorphism, not an isometry. With the standard H^1 norm (||v||_{L^2}^2+||v'||_{L^2}^2), the X_{H_0}-norm (|v(0)|^2+T||v'||^2)^{1/2} is only equivalent to it, with T-dependent constants. These constants degenerate as T->0 (|v(0)|^2 is not controlled uniformly) and grow with T. So the claimed equality is false, and the T-independent constants and (1+T)^gamma rates in the H^1 estimate do not follow.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Equip H^1(I,H) with the norm (|v(0)|^2+T||v'||_{L^2}^2)^{1/2}. This norm is equivalent to the standard one for fixed T, and the identity then holds exactly.
issues.overall_effect: The explicit T-dependence of the coercivity and continuity bounds in H^1 is unsupported. This affects the Céa-type estimate and Theorem th:Schro, which is stated in the same H^1 norm.
issues.title: Unestablished isometry between X_{H_0} and H^1(I,H) behind the T-independent constants
issues.why_classification: A one-line choice of norm restores every stated estimate and rate unchanged; no new argument is needed.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof drops B from the residual and uses f=(i\partial_t-H)u^*. This is false when B is nonzero, since then (i\partial_t-H)u^*=f+Bu^*. It concludes F(v)=||u-u^*||_{X_H}^2 and invokes only part (i) of Theorem th: XX0 XX equality. So the B nonzero case, with gamma=2, is not proved.

issues.failure_explanation: S^* is defined with (i\partial_t-H-B(t)). The converse argument nevertheless identifies ((i\partial_t-H)e^{-itH}w|u) with <e^{-itH}w,S^*u>, which drops the B term. It then concludes (i\partial_t-H)u=f instead of (i\partial_t-H-B)u=f, so for nonzero B the 'if' direction is not proved. Separately, the definitions give S^*=S_0^*-(A+B), not S_0^*+A+B. The minus sign is the version used later in the proof of Corollary cor:L2.

issues.failure_explanation: In this section S^* contains B, and the claimed constants alpha/(1+T)^2 and C(1+T) are those of the B-dependent estimate. Yet E^* contains only A. The proof's identity u-(S_0^*)^{-1}Au=(S_0^*)^{-1}S^*u holds only when B=0. For nonzero B, E^* vanishes at the solution without B, not at u^*, so the two-sided bound around u^* fails.
